> Nothing escapes detection.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firestore](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firestore-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenStreetMap](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenStreetMap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We chose this project to address the persistent and real-world problem of unreliable mobile network connectivity. Despite the widespread adoption of advanced technologies like 4G and 5G, users still frequently experience signal drops in everyday environments such as basements, buildings, campuses, and crowded areas. This becomes especially critical in situations involving emergencies, where lack of connectivity can delay communication and compromise safety. Currently, there is no simple, real-time, user-driven system that helps individuals identify or navigate around such dead zones. Our solution aims to bridge this gap by collecting real-time signal data, visualizing weak network areas on a map, and guiding users toward better connectivity. By doing so, the system not only improves user awareness but also has the potential to scale into a crowd-sourced platform that can assist in smarter infrastructure planning and network optimization.

**Challenges we ran into**

Developing Deadzone Finder presented a series of complex technical hurdles, primarily the "communication gap" between the browser’s sandbox and the phone's cellular hardware, which we overcame by engineering a Capacitor Native Bridge to access Android’s Telephony Manager and utilizing network latency (RTT) as a telemetry fallback. We navigated a volatile build environment, resolving initial configuration conflicts between Vite and the newly released Tailwind CSS v4 engine through a live-stack migration, while simultaneously optimizing geospatial rendering to prevent hardware lag during real-time heatmap generation over the AOT Campus. Furthermore, we solved critical data-sync race conditions by implementing asynchronous lifecycle guards to ensure verified GPS locking before rendering, and refactored our local development environment to bypass cloud-sync file lockouts, ultimately resulting in a high-performance, hardware-integrated Android application that functions seamlessly in the physical world.

**OPEN INNOVATION**

Deadzone Finder epitomizes Open Innovation by disrupting the traditional top-down ISP monopoly and replacing it with a bottom-up, decentralized sensing mesh that democratizes network transparency. By orchestrating existing Android hardware into a global intelligence grid, we transform every smartphone into a passive telemetry node, shifting the power of data from multi-billion dollar corporations to the end-user. Our AOT Campus pilot serves as a high-density blueprint for hyper-local problem solving, proving that collective intelligence can map the invisible blind spots of the digital world more accurately and honestly than any static marketing map. This project creates a scalable, open-access ecosystem that provides critical utility not just for individuals, but as a foundational data layer for governments and safety innovators to build a truly signal-aware future where connectivity is treated as a transparent human right.

### LocalLens
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/locallens-ca85) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/iamanirbanbasak/binary_hack) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://gamma.app/docs/LocalLens--zjesbo16v0htq1w) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/8ba9e65b743c425099dd5862c6a84bf6) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-BINARY%20v2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://binaryvtwo.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Every word. Every decision. One memory.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chrome Extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Extension-333333?style=flat-square) ![Jira](https://img.shields.io/badge/Jira-333333?style=flat-square) ![chromadb](https://img.shields.io/badge/chromadb-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every day, your team generates enormous intelligence — architecture decisions, client promises, technical risks, action items. It lives in Telegram group chats, voice notes, Google Meet recordings, PDFs, and shared links.

**By tomorrow morning, 90% of it is gone.**

LocalLens is a multi-agent conversation intelligence engine that passively monitors every source your team communicates through and builds a living, queryable knowledge graph — so nothing important is ever lost again.

**What you can do with it:**

- **Ask anything about your team's history** — `/ask why did we choose Redis?` returns a sourced answer: *"Based on what @Raj said in a voice note on Mar 14..."*

- **Transcribe voice notes automatically** — Groq Whisper processes every voice message in real-time. Decisions made on voice notes are now searchable, attributable, and raiseable as Jira tickets.

- **Detect cross-team blind spots** — Deploy across multiple groups and LocalLens tells you: *"Dev has been blocked 5 days. Design doesn't know. The client expects delivery Friday. Nobody connected those dots."* Until now.

- **Turn signals into Jira tickets automatically** — Every recurring bug, blocker, or tech debt item detected in chat can be raised as a properly-described Jira ticket with one command — or automatically when severity is critical.

- **Process your meetings** — A Chrome extension captures Google Meet audio, transcribes it, and extracts decisions, action items, and blockers into the same knowledge graph as your Telegram signals.

- **Ingest any document** — PDFs, DOCX files, and links shared in the group are automatically chunked and stored in the RAG pipeline, queryable alongside chat.

**Who it's for:** Engineering teams, product squads, agencies, and any group of 3+ people making decisions in Telegram. Especially relevant for teams where voice notes carry more signal than text — which is most teams.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Multi-provider LLM fallback under rate limits**
We use 5 free LLM providers (Groq, Cerebras, SambaNova, OpenRouter, Google) with automatic fallback. The challenge was that each provider fails differently — some return 429s, some time out silently, some return malformed JSON. Building a router that handles all failure modes gracefully without losing a signal took significant iteration. Solution: unified error classification (rate_limit vs timeout vs hard error) with per-task-type provider priority queues.

**2. Groq Whisper + Telegram OGG format**
Telegram sends voice notes as OGG/Opus. Groq Whisper accepts OGG but the MIME type detection was inconsistent — the same bytes would succeed or fail depending on how the multipart form was constructed. Solution: explicit MIME type mapping from file extension and forcing the filename field in the multipart upload.

**3. Cross-group signal comparison without context collapse**
The cross-group analyst needs to compare signals from 3+ groups simultaneously without losing which signal came from which group. Early attempts collapsed everything into one context window and the LLM lost track of provenance. Solution: structured prompt with explicit group labeling per signal block and a JSON schema that forces per-group attribution in the output.

**4. Jira ADF (Atlassian Document Format)**
Jira Cloud's REST API v3 rejects plain text in description fields — it requires Atlassian Document Format (a nested JSON schema). This was under documented and caused silent 400 errors for two hours. Solution: built a `_text_to_adf()` converter that handles paragraphs and bullet lists, which now handles all LLM-generated ticket descriptions reliably.

**5. ChromaDB deduplication across signal sources**
With signals coming from chat, voice, Meet, documents, and links simultaneously, the same underlying fact could be extracted multiple times. Solution: a `jira_raised` tracking signal pattern in ChromaDB that stores the original signal ID as the document text, enabling O(1) deduplication lookups before any ticket is raised.

## Tracks Applied
🤖 Best Use of AI Agents
🗣️ Best Use of LLMs
🛠️ Best Developer Tool
📱 Best Use of Telegram API
🏆 Grand Prize / General Track

*(Select whichever of these match what the hackathon offers. "Best Use of AI Agents" is your strongest category — 8 specialized agents with a full agentic pipeline is exactly what that track is looking for.)*


## Technologies Used
Python 3.11, FastAPI, ChromaDB, Cohere Embed v4,
Groq (LLaMA 3.1 8B / 70B + Whisper Large v3),
Cerebras, SambaNova (LLaMA 405B), OpenRouter,
python-telegram-bot v21, httpx, React 18,
Tailwind CSS, Recharts, Jira REST API v3,
Chrome Extensions (Manifest V3), Web Speech API

## Platforms
Telegram, Google Meet, Jira (Atlassian), Chrome, Web

**AI/ML**

LocalLens is a production-grade multi-agent AI system built entirely on free
LLM inference. Eight specialized agents form an end-to-end pipeline:

- **Context Detector** — classifies group type (dev/product/client/community)
- **Signal Extractor** — identifies decisions, tech debt, bugs, promises, risks
- **Classifier** — tags severity, urgency, sentiment, entities
- **Entity Resolver** — deduplicates people and concepts across messages
- **Knowledge Architect** — maintains a living ChromaDB vector knowledge graph
- **Pattern Detector** — surfaces trends: recurring bugs, knowledge silos, tech debt spikes
- **Cross-Group Analyst** — detects blind spots *between* teams (our core differentiator)
- **Query Agent** — RAG-powered natural language Q&A with source attribution

**Multi-modal AI:** Groq Whisper (whisper-large-v3) transcribes Telegram voice
notes in real-time — the first team intelligence system to treat voice as a
first-class signal source.

**Multi-provider resilience:** Groq → Cerebras → SambaNova (405B) → OpenRouter
→ Google, with automatic fallback on rate limits. Total free capacity: ~10,000
LLM calls/day at $0 cost.

**Vector RAG:** Cohere Embed v4 embeddings stored in ChromaDB, with semantic
retrieval across chat, voice, documents, links, and Google Meet transcripts.

**Open Innovation**

LocalLens solves a problem that affects every team on Earth: the knowledge
your team generates in conversation is invisible to every tool that exists.

**The innovation:** We are the first system to unify five communication sources
— Telegram chat, voice notes, Google Meet recordings, shared documents, and
URLs — into a single queryable knowledge graph with full provenance tracking.

**Why it's novel:**
- Every competitor (Slack AI, Prism, Runbear) is text-only and reactive.
  LocalLens is multi-modal and proactive.
- Cross-group intelligence has no prior art: no product detects blind spots
  *between* teams automatically.
- Voice note intelligence is completely unaddressed in the market despite voice
  notes carrying the most critical decisions in real teams — especially in
  non-western and informal team cultures.

**Real-world impact:** A team using LocalLens never loses an architecture
decision, a client promise, or a critical blocker to the scroll. The system
gets smarter the longer it runs — every new message makes the knowledge graph
richer, not just the history longer.

**Built entirely on free infrastructure:** $0 in API costs. Deployable by any
team with a Telegram group and a free Groq account. The barrier to adoption
is zero.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional mesh networks (like BLE ) suffer from network flooding and high latency when scaling to thousands of nodes. Standard routing protocols are "blind"—they don't account for the physical movement of nodes (drift), leading to broken paths, or they assign static Time-to-Live (TTL) values that either drop packets too early or cause "zombie packets" that clog the bandwidth. Furthermore, in highly mobile environments, a path optimized at one moment is often physically impossible by the next, requiring a routing system that is both predictive and spatially aware.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/7b7a580d2c204a989c2e1a4f2c5878fb/57cc06a2-d603-4e08-b607-fd17b873a794.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/7b7a580d2c204a989c2e1a4f2c5878fb/8c992868-38b5-4d81-b574-31fb56342eb8.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/7b7a580d2c204a989c2e1a4f2c5878fb/c5ea1e60-497b-4ba0-a488-6a2957538b77.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/7b7a580d2c204a989c2e1a4f2c5878fb/a1a88531-42fc-4592-8849-13591cdba2ce.png)

IntelliSynapse solves this by removing the middleman. It turns every user's device into a microscopic, independent router, weaving a decentralized mesh network via Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). However, building a Mobile Ad-hoc Network (MANET) introduces three massive engineering challenges that standard routing algorithms fail to handle. IntelliSynapse solves all of them:

**1. The "Broadcast Storm"**

The Problem: In standard mesh networks, if a user shifts in their chair, the network floods that tiny movement update to thousands of devices. This "broadcast storm" completely drains phone batteries and clogs the BLE bandwidth, leaving no room for actual chat messages.

The MeshChat Solution: We engineered the Elastic Horizon Algorithm (Movement Threshold Gate). The system dynamically calculates physical drift. If a node moves less than 15% of its BLE range (a micro-movement), the network silently absorbs the noise. The system only triggers a central topology update when a node physically breaks its local perimeter, saving massive amounts of battery and network overhead.
**
2. The "Moving Target" (Mid-Flight Packet Loss)**

The Problem: Real people don't stand still. In standard routing (like A* or Dijkstra), the route is calculated the moment you hit "Send." If a person acting as a middle-hop (a courier) walks out of range while the packet is mid-flight, the link snaps and the packet is dropped.

The IntelliSynapse: We implemented D Lite routing with Mid-Flight Replanning*. If a link breaks while a message is in transit, MeshChat doesn't drop the packet. Instead, it freezes the packet at the last connected node, instantly recalculates a local detour based on the surviving physical topology, and seamlessly resumes delivery. The sender and receiver never even know a link broke.

**3. Fragile Links & Dead Ends**

The Problem: Devices constantly drift in and out of the absolute edge of Bluetooth range, creating weak connections that are highly likely to drop packets.

The MeshChat Solution: MeshChat uses an Adaptive Time-To-Live (TTL). The algorithm evaluates the physical RSSI (signal strength) of every hop on a planned route. If the algorithm detects a weak link, it proactively assigns the packet a higher TTL "lifespan" so it can survive the inevitable D* Lite recalculations without timing out.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Data Scale and Memory Management
Attempting to build a global physical graph for 1,000,000 nodes using standard libraries resulted in a critical memory failure. The number of potential connections in a dataset of that size was too large for the system to process at once. You solved this by implementing Time-Slicing and Spatial Chunking, which filtered the data into specific time windows and reduced the active node count per simulation to a manageable size.

2. Temporal Inconsistency and Node Mobility
In a real-world dataset, nodes are constantly moving. A path that was perfectly optimized at the start of a transmission often became physically impossible by the time the packet reached the middle of the network. To fix this, you moved away from a static calculation model to a Self-Healing Corridor that acknowledges node drift in real-time without crashing the entire routing protocol.

3. API and Network Overhead
Initially, every single hop in the mesh network was attempting to send a report to the central server. In a massive simulation, this caused extreme latency and would have crashed a real-world IoT network. You navigated this by architecting an Edge-First Telemetry system where nodes cache their data in a Local Ledger and only perform bulk uploads to the cloud during specific intervals or critical events.

4. Hybrid Quantum-Classical Integration
Quantum simulators are highly efficient at searching through possibilities but struggle with processing raw, unorganized geographic data. You overcame this by building a Ghost Packet Architecture. You used classical algorithms to discover a small set of candidate paths and then fed only those specific candidates into the Quantum Search engine to amplify the best route.

5. Geofencing Rigidity
Strict geofences are often too fragile for mobile networks; if a node moves a few meters out of a zone, dropping the packet immediately causes unnecessary data loss. You solved this by implementing a Two-Hop Grace Period. This allowed for "soft violations" where a packet could temporarily exit the safety corridor to find a way back in, only triggering a permanent drop and server report if the violation persisted.

**AI/ML**

Our project implements a Hybrid Quantum-Classical Intelligence stack to optimize dynamic BLE mesh networks through three sophisticated layers:

Graph Neural Networks (GraphSAGE): We use GraphSAGE to generate 32-dimensional structural embeddings. By sampling and aggregating neighbor features, the model predicts Link Reliability and Packet Drop Probability across a 1-million-node topology, allowing the network to "learn" its own congestion patterns.

Quantum Optimization (Grover’s Algorithm): To solve the complex routing problem in dense environments, we utilize Qiskit to run a Quantum Grover’s Search. This acts as an Oracle to mathematically amplify and select the most efficient path from candidate routes, significantly reducing the computational overhead of classical pathfinding.

Tiered Spatial Enforcement:
Tier 1 (Autonomous Ledger): Every node monitors its own 3km circular radius. If it drifts beyond this anchor, it self-logs the coordinates and resets its boundary, triggering a GraphSAGE re-embedding.

Tier 2 (Corridor Geo-fencing): The system defines a "Gross Area" around the optimized quantum path. If a packet is hijacked or deviates for more than 2 hops, the AI triggers a mandatory drop and reports the anomaly.

**Open Innovation**

Our project embodies Open Innovation by bridging the gap between theoretical Quantum Computing and practical IoT/BLE Mesh Networking. We address the universal challenge of maintaining reliable communications in dense, highly dynamic environments where traditional routing protocols fail due to high packet-drop rates and node mobility.

Innovation Highlights:
Cross-Domain Integration: We’ve built a unique "Intelligence Stack" that combines Graph Machine Learning (GraphSAGE) for structural node analysis with Quantum Search Algorithms (Grover’s) for ultra-efficient path selection.

Decentralized Spatial Management: We introduce a Tiered Spatial Ledger system. Every node is self-aware of its 3km circular radius, autonomously logging its drift and updating its geo-anchor without the need for a central control overhead.

Security & Resilience: The "Gross Area" geo-fencing (Tier 2) acts as a high-level kill-switch, dropping hijacked or aberrant packets after 2 hops, creating a self-healing network architecture that prioritizes data integrity.

This project is a blueprint for the next generation of smart-city infrastructure, emergency response networks, and decentralized drone communication, providing a scalable, AI-driven solution to a global connectivity problem.

> Your academic legacy, Verified

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![pinata](https://img.shields.io/badge/pinata-333333?style=flat-square) ![Algorand](https://img.shields.io/badge/Algorand-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

By the time a student graduates, every project they built has vanished onto a local hard drive. Every syllabus a professor uploaded to a temporary Google Drive link is dead.

For professors: No immutable record of what was published on Day 1 — leading to disputes over deadlines and rubrics.
For students: No way to prove to a recruiter that their GitHub project is original and timestamped.
For institutions: Years of intellectual capital lost to server crashes and expired accounts.

We built TraceHub for this. It is a unified upload platform for academic institutions. When a professor or student uploads a document:

The file is stored on Pinata (IPFS) — content-addressed, decentralized storage where the file's URL is its own hash, making tampering self-evident.
A 0-ALGO transaction is minted on Algorand Testnet, encoding a SHA-256 content hash, uploader name, and timestamp into the blockchain as an immutable record.
Everything is saved to MongoDB Atlas and surfaced on a clean dashboard.
The result: a permanent, blockchain-timestamped academic archive where any tampering with MongoDB is cryptographically detectable — the on-chain hash won't match.

**Challenges we ran into**

The challenges that we faced included finding a decentralized database, solved by Pinata(IPFS). Another challenge that we faced was integrating mongoDB a centralized database system because it is cost effective and decentralized database Pinata and notary Algorand for securing the actual data from tampering in the future or even if the tampering happens the previous versions will always have a backup for the data so no loss happens.

**Web3**

The project leverages Algorand blockchain as an immutable notary service—when professors or students upload academic resources, a 0-ALGO transaction is minted encoding the file's SHA-256 content hash, uploader identity, and timestamp onto the Algorand Testnet, making any tampering with the MongoDB database cryptographically detectable by comparing the on-chain hash with the database record. Files themselves are stored decentralized on IPFS via Pinata's pinning service, where the content-addressed URL serves as its own integrity proof. Additionally, the project includes AlgoKit-based TypeScript smart contracts (currently in development) to enable custom on-chain logic, creating a three-layer Web3 stack: Algorand for timestamped verification, IPFS for tamper-evident storage, and smart contracts for extensible academic verification logic.

**Algorand**

Algorand has been used in this project as the notary and verification system to register any change, update or creation of any document, material or resources.

**Education**

This system is specifically designed for students, professors of colleges and universities to maintain their intellectual properties with version updates and protect data from tampering in the future using the web3 technology.

**The problem it solves**

## 🛡️ Scam-Shield – Digital Certainty for a Modern India

In a rapidly digitizing India, scams have evolved beyond simple phishing emails into complex, multi-channel attacks involving WhatsApp messages, fake investment calls, malicious QR codes, and sophisticated spoofed URLs. Most existing security tools are too technical or only focus on one area (e.g., just antivirus or just URL blocking).

**Scam-Shield** provides a unified, AI-powered defense system that serves as a **"Sanity Check for the Digital World."**

---

### 🔍 Key Features

#### 🔹 Multi-Modal Detection
Users can analyze suspicious:
- Text messages  
- URLs  
- Screenshots  
- Voice notes  

All in one platform for complete protection.

---

#### 🔹 Explainable Risk Intelligence
Instead of a "black box" verdict, Scam-Shield provides:
- A transparent **risk score**
- Breakdown based on:
  - Urgency indicators  
  - Social engineering patterns  
  - Technical signals  

---

#### 🔹 Empowering Victims
For users who have already been scammed, the platform helps by:
- Generating a **legal-ready Fraud Timeline**
- Simplifying reporting to cybercrime authorities  
- Organizing evidence in a structured format  

---

#### 🔹 Community Awareness
- Real-time **threat map** across India  
- Identifies scam hotspots  
- Converts individual reports into **community-wide protection**

---

### 🌍 Vision
To create a safer digital ecosystem where every user can verify before they trust.

Integrating high-end interactive shaders (like our WebGL Orb and FloatingLines) in a React environment without:
- Impacting page load speed

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

In today’s fast-paced world, people constantly generate ideas, make decisions, and consume information — but most of it is lost due to lack of capture, organization, and recall.

Traditional tools like notes apps, task managers, or chatbots require **manual effort**, forcing users to stop what they’re doing, switch context, and input information. This leads to:

- Lost ideas and forgotten insights  
- Scattered information across multiple platforms  
- Time wasted in searching and reconstructing past context  
- Cognitive overload from trying to remember everything  
- Inefficient decision-making due to lack of accessible knowledge  

Brain.2 solves this by acting as an **ambient intelligence layer** that works in the background:

- Automatically captures conversations, ideas, and decisions  
- Organizes information into a structured personal knowledge system  
- Provides instant, contextual answers across all past data  
- Generates daily insights without requiring manual reflection  
- Eliminates the need for constant note-taking and task tracking  

Instead of managing tools, users can focus purely on **thinking, creating, and deciding** — while Brain.2 handles memory, organization, and retrieval.

In short, Brain.2 transforms fragmented information into **continuous, compounding intelligence**.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I ran into

Building Brain.2 involved solving multiple complex challenges across AI, infrastructure, and user experience:

### 1. Real-time ambient processing
Handling continuous voice input (up to several hours daily) while maintaining low latency and accuracy was a major challenge.  
**Solution:** Implemented chunk-based processing with intelligent segmentation using Hugging Face models and optimized pipelines to process only meaningful segments instead of raw continuous streams.

---

### 2. Cost optimization at scale
Always-on audio processing, embeddings, and LLM calls significantly increased infrastructure costs.  
**Solution:** Introduced selective processing, batching, and compression strategies. Reduced redundant embedding generation and optimized API usage to keep the system sustainable.

---

### 3. Context retrieval accuracy
Ensuring that the system returns the *right* information from a growing knowledge base was difficult.  
**Solution:** Designed a structured vector search pipeline using Pinecone with metadata filtering and improved chunking strategies for better semantic relevance.

---

### 4. Multimodal data handling
Managing text, audio, images, and documents in a unified system required consistent indexing and retrieval logic.  
**Solution:** Built a normalized data pipeline with MongoDB for structured storage and vector embeddings for semantic linking across all formats.

---

### 5. User experience vs automation balance
Creating a system that feels “invisible” yet reliable was challenging — too much automation can feel uncontrollable.  
**Solution:** Added controlled interaction modes (Send Mode, Ask Mode) along with transparency in insights, giving users both automation and control.

---

### 6. Scalability & performance
As user data grows, maintaining fast query responses and system performance becomes harder.  
**Solution:** Used efficient indexing, caching strategies, and scalable backend architecture to ensure consistent performance.

---

Overall, the biggest challenge was balancing **intelligence, cost, and usability** — ensuring Brain.2 remains powerful without becoming complex or expensive.

**AI/ML**

## AI/ML Track Fit

Brain.2 is an AI-native system built on ambient intelligence, multimodal understanding, and real-time contextual learning.

At its core, the product leverages multiple AI/ML components:

- **Natural Language Processing (NLP):** Powered by Groq API, enabling fast and efficient language understanding, reasoning, and response generation across user data.
- **Speech-to-Text & Audio Processing:** Uses Groq’s transcription capabilities along with AI-based voice segmentation to convert real-world conversations into structured knowledge.
- **Vector Embeddings & Semantic Search:** Embedding models are used to transform text and voice into vectors, stored in a vector database for context-aware retrieval.
- **Multimodal Learning:** Integrates text, voice, images, and documents into a unified knowledge system for deeper understanding.
- **Contextual Query Engine:** Users can query their entire knowledge base in natural language and receive precise, AI-generated insights.

A key innovation is the **continuous learning loop**, where the system becomes more accurate and personalized as it captures more data over time.

By combining Groq’s high-speed inference with vector search and multimodal processing, Brain.2 goes beyond traditional AI tools and acts as a **persistent intelligence layer** that transforms unstructured real-world data into actionable insights.

**Open Innovation**

## Open Innovation Track Fit

Brain.2 fits strongly into the Open Innovation track by introducing a completely new paradigm of interacting with technology — shifting from manual tools to an **ambient, AI-driven intelligence layer**.

Unlike traditional productivity or note-taking systems, Brain.2 eliminates the need for active input and organization. It passively captures real-world data (conversations, ideas, documents) and transforms it into structured, actionable knowledge using AI.

This approach enables:

- **Zero-friction interaction** — users no longer need to manage tools manually  
- **Cross-domain applicability** — usable by students, professionals, researchers, and organizations  
- **New human-computer interaction model** — moving from command-based systems to continuous, context-aware intelligence  
- **Scalable innovation** — can evolve into team intelligence systems, enterprise knowledge layers, and decision-support platforms  

Brain.2 is not just an improvement over existing tools — it redefines how humans store, retrieve, and utilize knowledge.

By combining ambient computing, AI, and multimodal data processing, the project opens up new possibilities for building **intelligence-first systems** that can be applied across industries, making it a strong fit for Open Innovation.

### Phantom AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/phantom-ai-32c5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/VishwasSharma28/TeamTryhardsPhantomProof.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://team-tryhards-phantom-proof.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/watch?v=_kpUFVTkmDs&feature=shared) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack--Nocturne%202.O-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-nocturne-2.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turning Claims into Verified Truth

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/OCR-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![OSINT](https://img.shields.io/badge/OSINT-333333?style=flat-square) ![ELA](https://img.shields.io/badge/ELA-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The internet today is flooded with manipulated images, fake screenshots, AI-generated media, and fraudulent digital evidence, making it increasingly difficult for people to determine what is real and what is fake. Fake payment receipts are often used to scam individuals, AI-generated images can spread misinformation, and altered screenshots of news or messages can mislead large audiences. Most existing verification tools provide only a simple “real or fake” result without explaining why something is suspicious, leaving users uncertain about whether they can trust the result.

Phantom AI solves this by acting as a digital verification system for online content. Users can upload images, screenshots, or digital documents, and the system performs a multi-stage forensic investigation that analyzes pixel-level artifacts, extracts text using OCR, checks for manipulation patterns, and verifies contextual claims. Instead of giving a vague answer, the platform generates a structured verification report with evidence, confidence scores, and explanations, helping users understand the reasoning behind the verdict.

This makes tasks such as fact-checking images, verifying payment screenshots, detecting AI-generated content, and identifying misinformation significantly easier and safer. By providing transparent evidence and automated analysis, Phantom AI helps journalists, investigators, businesses, and everyday users quickly verify suspicious digital content and avoid fraud or misinformation.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/723c1bae3eb847359e74f711251d24b6/5e21d27b-4337-43b8-bcbc-b7a08e771f3a.jpeg)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/723c1bae3eb847359e74f711251d24b6/dee07096-8be7-4137-a113-70160344f94d.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/723c1bae3eb847359e74f711251d24b6/0eec5b74-c46f-4a75-aad9-d47c1ae7d840.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/723c1bae3eb847359e74f711251d24b6/bef5a47c-47cf-473b-9d79-3783fba59134.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Phantom AI involved several technical and practical challenges across the detection pipelines, model accuracy, and deployment infrastructure. Since the system integrates multiple AI verification engines, ensuring that all components worked reliably together required careful debugging and iteration.

1. OCR Context Limitations in Payment Fraud Detection

One major challenge occurred in the payment screenshot verification module. Many payment screenshots contain very limited textual context, and the OCR engine sometimes extracted only partial information such as the amount or fragments of a transaction ID. Because of this, the fraud detection logic initially produced inconsistent or inaccurate results, especially when key fields like bank name or transaction status were missing.

To address this, we implemented research-based pattern assumptions based on common structures used in legitimate UPI and bank payment interfaces. We introduced validation checks for expected fields such as UTR format, transaction layout patterns, amount structure, and known UI elements commonly present in authentic payment receipts. By combining these heuristic checks with OCR output, we significantly improved the reliability of the payment verification results.

2. Misinformation Detection and Fact-Checking Accuracy

Another challenge appeared in the misinformation detection pipeline. Initially, the system struggled to reliably verify extracted claims because screenshots often contained short headlines or incomplete statements, which made fact-checking difficult. This sometimes caused the system to miss relevant references when querying external sources.

We improved this by refining our OSINT verification pipeline and integrating RSS-based live fact-check feeds. Instead of relying on a single lookup method, the system now performs multiple contextual checks using extracted keywords and semantic matching. These adjustments allowed the system to identify related fact-check articles more accurately and improved the credibility of the verification results.

3. Model Hosting and Deployment Constraints

Deployment was another major hurdle. Our system relied on multiple machine learning models for image analysis, OCR, and semantic verification, which created memory and resource constraints when hosting the backend. Some cloud platforms limit available RAM and compute resources, making it difficult to run several models simultaneously.

To solve this, we redesigned the deployment architecture by separating responsibilities between services. The backend API handles orchestration and lightweight processing, while heavier AI models are hosted externally and accessed through inference APIs. This hybrid deployment approach allowed the system to remain stable while still supporting multiple verification pipelines.

4. Integrating Multiple Detection Pipelines

Because Phantom AI supports deepfake detection, misinformation verification, and payment fraud analysis, maintaining clean separation between these pipelines was essential. Early prototypes had tightly coupled logic, which caused conflicts when different detection modules were triggered.

We resolved this by designing independent endpoints and modular services for each detection type, ensuring that each pipeline runs only when selected through the frontend toggle. This made the architecture easier to maintain, debug, and scale.

### ResQNav
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/resqnav-e5bf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Victorralph7011/ResQNav) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1yJgDu1mq4iqWHSHgLWs7wl48c6Wb4nuBpwnY-LikZSs/edit?usp=sharing) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/ff7a2c353b5b42ed89ed520bcf2361b1) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackNova%203.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknova-3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Take a Path. Save a Life.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Have you ever sat in bumper-to-bumper traffic, only to hear the desperate wail of an ambulance stuck right behind you? Every year, cities lose billions of hours to traffic gridlock. But when an emergency vehicle gets trapped in that same traffic, we don't just lose time—we lose lives.

Currently, popular navigation apps are "selfish." They optimize routes for the individual driver. When a sudden accident occurs, everyone is routed into the same adjacent streets, creating massive bottlenecks that paralyze emergency response times.

How ResQNav Fixes This-
ResQNav bridges the gap between everyday commuters and emergency dispatchers by acting as a synchronized brain for city traffic. We shift the paradigm from passive navigation to active traffic management.

For Emergency Responders: Instead of fighting through congestion, ResQNav creates a dynamic "Green Corridor." As soon as an incident is verified, the system actively pushes public traffic away from the ambulance's route, giving first responders a clear, unobstructed path to the victims.

For Daily Commuters: Nobody wants to be stuck in a jam. ResQNav proactively sends "Take this path, save a life" notifications to drivers approaching an accident zone. It instantly calculates smart detours that keep them moving and out of the rescue team's way.

For City Infrastructure: It eliminates the chaos of unverified, noisy accident reports. By using our Gemini AI chatbot to instantly verify crowdsourced images of crashes, we ensure dispatchers and routing engines only react to real emergencies.

In short: ResQNav stops treating traffic as just an inconvenience. It actively manages the roads so daily commuters save time, and emergency responders can save lives.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Simulating A* Avoidance Routing
One of our biggest hurdles was figuring out how to dynamically reroute traffic around a live accident. Standard free routing APIs (like OSRM) don't allow you to block specific GPS coordinates on the fly. We overcame this by writing a custom "Forced Waypoint" algorithm. It mathematically calculates a safe offset distance from the crash site and forces the routing engine to draw a sweeping detour path completely around the incident.

2. State Syncing & AI Rate Limits
Connecting our Gemini AI verification sequence directly to the live MapLibre interface caused initial UI re-render issues. We solved this by building a tightly controlled state sequence using Framer Motion to ensure the toasts and map markers appeared cinematically. We also had to implement graceful error handling for 503 Service Unavailable spikes from the AI API so our live presentation would remain bulletproof.

> Generative AI-Powered SOC Assistanted Log Analysis

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Git](https://img.shields.io/badge/Git-333333?style=flat-square) ![ngrok](https://img.shields.io/badge/ngrok-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern organizations generate massive volumes of security logs from firewalls, servers, and applications. Manually analyzing these logs is time-consuming, error-prone, and requires expert knowledge. This often leads to alert fatigue, missed threats, and delayed incident response.

SentinelAI addresses this by transforming raw, complex logs into structured, human-readable security insights. Instead of manually parsing logs, users can upload a file and instantly receive:

- A clear incident summary in plain English
- A reconstructed timeline of suspicious activity
- Mapping of observed behavior to MITRE ATT&CK tactics and techniques
- Contextual threat intelligence (e.g., IP reputation and location)
- Actionable remediation suggestions

This significantly reduces the time required for log analysis and makes security insights accessible even to non-experts, helping teams respond faster and more effectively to potential threats.[](url)[](url)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was handling inconsistencies in AI-generated responses.

Since the backend relies on an LLM to analyze logs and return structured JSON, the model would sometimes:
- Return improperly formatted JSON
- Include extra text outside the JSON
- Miss required fields like timeline or MITRE mappings

This caused parsing errors and broke the frontend rendering.

To solve this, I:
- Enforced strict output formatting using a detailed system prompt
- Used response_format={"type": "json_object"} to force valid JSON output
- Added error handling in the backend to catch and safely return failures

Another major challenge was CORS issues when deploying the frontend (GitHub Pages) and backend (Render). The frontend requests were blocked by the browser due to missing headers.

I fixed this by explicitly configuring FastAPI’s CORSMiddleware to allow requests from the deployed frontend domain.

Additionally, managing secrets (API keys) during GitHub deployment was a hurdle. GitHub blocked pushes due to exposed keys, which I resolved by:
- Moving secrets into environment variables
- Adding .env to .gitignore
- Using Render environment variables for secure deployment

**GenAI**

It combines an intelligent IDE, automated code review, multi-agent assistance, and real-time collaboration into one seamless platform. Developers can write, analyze, and improve code faster using AI agents that understand project context, detect issues, and suggest improvements across the entire codebase. ### Multiagent government scheme navigator
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/multiagent-government-scheme-navigator-0549) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AbhimanyuSingh35/scheme-navigator) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1z9TB4SALAKAc264drs0gpCIgQeRmSCno) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/erCOxVi9RkQ) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Electrothon%208.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://electrothon-8.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-3-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Let AI Find the Schemes You Deserve.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Translation API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Translation%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ai Agents](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ai%20Agents-333333?style=flat-square) ![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Despite the Indian government launching thousands of welfare schemes to support farmers, students, women entrepreneurs, small businesses, rural citizens, and elderly people, a large portion of the population still does not benefit from them. The core issue is not the lack of schemes but the difficulty in discovering, understanding, and applying for them. Information about these schemes is scattered across multiple government portals, eligibility criteria are often complex and difficult to interpret, and many citizens face language barriers when accessing English-only platforms. Additionally, the application process can be confusing and discouraging, especially for people unfamiliar with digital systems. On top of that, fraudulent intermediaries and fake schemes sometimes mislead citizens, causing them to lose money or trust in the system. Our solution simplifies this entire process by acting as an AI-powered assistant that helps citizens discover schemes they are eligible for, clearly understand the benefits, receive step-by-step guidance on how to apply, interact in their local language, and avoid fraudulent schemes. By bringing all this information together in one intelligent platform, our system makes government welfare programs more accessible, transparent, and easier to use, ensuring that the benefits actually reach the people who need them the most.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the major hurdles we encountered during development was related to the latency and inefficiency caused by sequential AI agents. Initially, our architecture passed the user query through multiple agents one after another, where each agent processed the entire context and forwarded it to the next agent. While this approach worked functionally, it introduced two major issues. First, the response time became slow because every agent had to process a large amount of context before generating an output. Second, sending excessive or irrelevant context to the language model increased the chances of hallucination, especially when using models like **Gemini**, which could sometimes generate answers based on unrelated information present in the prompt.

To address this problem, we implemented a vectorless search-based retrieval approach that filters and retrieves only the most relevant schemes before passing them to the AI agents. Instead of sending the entire dataset of government schemes to the model, we perform a lightweight retrieval step based on key attributes extracted from the user profile, such as occupation, state, income level, and land ownership. This ensures that only **relevant scheme information** is passed to the downstream agents. By minimizing unnecessary context, we significantly reduced hallucination and improved both **response accuracy and system speed**.

Another major challenge we faced was the **integration and coordination of multiple AI agents using MCP (Model Context Protocol)**. Since each agent had a specific role—such as profile understanding, eligibility checking, scheme discovery, fraud detection, and application guidance—we needed a reliable way to manage the flow of information between them. Ensuring that all agents could access a shared user context, communicate efficiently, and execute in the correct order required careful orchestration. We resolved this by designing a structured shared state and standardized message format through MCP, allowing agents to exchange only the required information. This helped us create a **coordinated multi-agent pipeline** where each agent contributes its specialized task without causing context overload or communication conflicts.
These challenges ultimately helped us refine our architecture, resulting in a system that is faster, more accurate, and better structured for scaling to real-world usage.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

Our project aligns strongly with the Hackathon Winner Track because it addresses a large real-world problem using a technically innovative and scalable solution. In India, thousands of government welfare schemes exist, yet millions of eligible citizens fail to benefit from them due to lack of awareness, complex eligibility criteria, language barriers, and complicated application processes. By building an AI-powered multi-agent assistant, we directly tackle this gap and create a system that can meaningfully improve access to public welfare.

From a technical perspective, the project demonstrates advanced AI system design rather than a simple chatbot. We implemented a multi-agent architecture where specialized agents handle different tasks such as profile understanding, eligibility verification, scheme discovery, fraud detection, benefit ranking, and application guidance. These agents collaborate through a shared context using MCP (Model Context Protocol), enabling a structured and modular pipeline where each agent performs a specific role efficiently.

We also introduced retrieval optimization through vectorless search, which ensures that only relevant schemes are passed to the language model. This reduces unnecessary context, improves response speed, and minimizes hallucination when using models like Gemini. Such architectural decisions demonstrate thoughtful engineering to make the system reliable, scalable, and production-ready.

In addition, the solution focuses heavily on real-world usability. Features like local language support, conversational memory, fraud detection, and step-by-step application guidance make the platform accessible to rural citizens and first-time digital users. This ensures that the technology is not only innovative but also inclusive and impactful for society.
Overall, our project combines social impact, technical depth, scalable architecture, and practical usability, which are key factors typically considered in hackathon winner tracks. By bridging the gap between government welfare programs and the citizens they are meant to serve, this system demonstrates how AI can be used to create meaningful, real-world impact at scale.

**IQ AI**

Our project, the AI-Powered Government Scheme Navigator, is a fully agent-native system built to solve one of India's most persistent civic problems — millions of eligible citizens missing out on government welfare schemes like PM-KISAN, Ayushman Bharat, PMAY, and hundreds of state-level programs simply because the process of discovering, verifying, and applying for them is too complex, opaque, and prone to fraud. To solve this, we designed a multi-agent architecture where every layer of the system is driven by a specialized, autonomous agent working in coordination through a central orchestrator, making it a direct and comprehensive fit for the IQ AI Agent Development Kit track. The first agent, the Profile Understanding Agent, takes raw unstructured natural language from the user — something as informal as "I am a 45-year-old farmer from Himachal Pradesh earning around ₹80,000 a year with two children" — and reasons over it to extract a clean, structured user profile with fields like occupation, state, income bracket, and family composition, demonstrating true semantic reasoning rather than keyword matching. The second agent, the Scheme Discovery and Eligibility Agent, takes that profile and evaluates it against a large corpus of government schemes across multiple eligibility dimensions including income thresholds, occupational categories, geographic applicability, age, gender, and caste considerations, returning only the schemes the user genuinely qualifies for. The third agent, the Benefit Ranking and Application Guide Agent, then takes those filtered results and ranks them by the real value they offer to that specific user, generating a personalized step-by-step application guide complete with required documents, portal links, and actionable instructions. The fourth agent, the Fraud Detection Agent, runs independently on every request and evaluates schemes and user inputs for signs of fraud — suspicious portals, impersonation patterns, and unusually inflated benefit claims — surfacing warnings before any action is taken, which represents a genuine safety and trust layer embedded into the agentic pipeline. The fifth and most technically sophisticated agent is the Assisted Apply Agent, which does not merely tell users what to do but actively prepares their application, pre-fills their data, identifies required documents, and guides them through the actual government portal using a suspend-and-resume lifecycle — it pauses when the user must take a real-world action like logging in with their Aadhaar credentials, holds its full state, and resumes exactly where it left off once the user signals readiness, implementing the Human-in-the-Loop agentic pattern that represents the frontier of real-world agent deployment. All five agents are coordinated by our orchestrator, which serves as the central nervous system of the system, managing agent sequencing, collecting real-time progress signals through the AgentProgress interface, streaming live status updates to the frontend via Server-Sent Events, aggregating results from all agents into a single coherent NavigatorResult, and making runtime decisions such as waiting until the conversational profile collector has gathered sufficient information before triggering the downstream pipeline. We have also implemented both major agentic interaction paradigms within the same system — a one-shot task-completion flow for the Quick Search tab where all agents run in sequence and results stream back in real time, and a stateful multi-turn conversational flow for the Chat tab where a session-persistent agent progressively collects the user's profile across multiple exchanges before handing off to the main pipeline, demonstrating architectural depth and a thorough understanding of how real-world agentic systems must operate across different user contexts. The table below summarises exactly how each ADK capability maps to our implementation.

**Best Use of Gemini 3 [Google Deepmind]**

Our application is built entirely on the Gemini 3 API as its core reasoning engine, powering every intelligent layer of the system. Here is how we leverage Gemini 3's most powerful features:
Multimodal Reasoning is used by our Profile Understanding Agent, which processes not just plain text but can interpret uploaded documents like income certificates, ration cards, and identity proofs to automatically extract and verify user profile data — eliminating manual entry entirely and making the system accessible even to users with low digital literacy.
Long Context Window is central to our Scheme Discovery Agent, which feeds Gemini 3 a large, detailed corpus of hundreds of central and state government schemes alongside the user's full profile in a single context window, enabling it to perform deep cross-referencing and eligibility reasoning across an enormous knowledge base in one pass — something no previous model generation could do reliably.
Deep Think (Advanced Reasoning) powers our Benefit Ranking and Fraud Detection Agents, where the model must weigh multiple competing factors — benefit value, application complexity, scheme authenticity, portal credibility — and arrive at nuanced, explainable decisions rather than surface-level matches. Instruction Following and Structured Output capabilities allow every agent to return clean, machine-readable JSON responses that flow seamlessly through our multi-agent orchestrator pipeline, enabling reliable agent-to-agent communication and consistent frontend rendering.
What makes our integration genuinely innovative is that Gemini 3 is not a feature in our application — it is the application. Every agent in our five-agent pipeline — profile extraction, scheme discovery, guide generation, fraud detection, and assisted application — is a targeted Gemini 3 prompt carefully engineered to perform a specific cognitive task, chained together by our orchestrator into a system that reasons, decides, and acts on behalf of citizens who have historically been excluded from the welfare systems designed to help them. The result is a production-grade, agent-native product that uses Gemini 3's most advanced capabilities to solve a real, large-scale civic problem affecting hundreds of millions of people across India.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sivoicenet-ai-919f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/gokul-raj-27/project-ai) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/lCDY1Fiw0jY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackVerse:%20Into%20the%20Web-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackverse-into-the-web.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turning Signs into Voices, Connecting People.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Communication between sign-language users and people who do not understand sign language can be difficult. SivoiceNet AI aims to reduce this communication gap by using a standard camera and AI-based sign recognition.

The current system provides a sign-language alphabet learning and recognition feature, allowing users to practice alphabet gestures and receive the recognized result in real time.

The planned system will extend this into:

Dynamic sign recognition using LSTM to understand hand movements across multiple video frames.
Written-text recognition using OCR as an additional communication input.
Context-aware communication by processing recognized signs into meaningful text.
A two-way communication workflow between sign-language users and non-signers.

The goal is to make sign-language interaction more accessible without requiring specialized hardware such as gloves, sensors, or dedicated devices.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our main challenges was getting reliable hand landmark data from different camera positions, hand orientations, and lighting conditions. Small changes in hand position could affect the extracted landmarks and, consequently, the recognition result.

Another challenge was preparing the dataset in a consistent format for model training. We addressed this by using MediaPipe landmarks as structured input instead of relying directly on raw images.

We also had to distinguish between static and dynamic signs. Alphabet gestures can often be recognized from a single frame, while dynamic signs require information from multiple frames. This led us to plan the use of LSTM for learning movement patterns across a sequence of landmarks.

As the project develops, we are also separating OCR from sign recognition, since OCR is intended for written text rather than hand gestures. This keeps each component focused on its specific task.

> Your Moment. Your Vibe. Your Caption.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our biggest challenges was making Rizz generate captions that actually feel personal and relevant, rather than generic AI-generated text. Understanding the context of an uploaded image, combining it with the user's thoughts, selected vibe, language, and content type—such as a Post, Reel, or Story—required careful prompt and logic design.

Another challenge was supporting multiple languages and mixed-language styles, especially Roman Urdu and Urdu + English, while keeping the captions natural and culturally relevant.

We overcame these challenges by improving the AI context flow: Photo + User Thought + Selected Vibe + Language + Content Format. Instead of sending a simple “generate a caption” request, we structured the input so the AI receives clear context about the user's intention and desired output. This helped us produce more personalized, natural, and platform-specific content.

We also faced challenges around image upload handling, validation, and maintaining a smooth user experience. We addressed these by adding file-format and size validation and keeping the generation flow simple and fast.

**The problem it solves**

Creating content for social media takes more time than people realize. Users often spend 10–30 minutes thinking about what caption to write, how to express their feelings, what tone to use, and whether the content matches their photo, Reel, or Story. Many people struggle with writer’s block, language barriers, repetitive captions, and finding the right words for the right moment.

Rizz makes this process instant and effortless. Users simply upload a photo, add a thought or context, choose their vibe and language, and Rizz generates personalized content that matches their moment.

People can use Rizz for:

📸 Photo captions for Instagram and other social platforms

🎬 Reels content that matches the video’s mood and context

📱 Story captions and quotes

💭 Turning simple thoughts or emotions into engaging social content

🌍 Creating content in English, Urdu, Roman Urdu, Urdu + English, Punjabi, and other local languages

✨ Generating captions based on specific vibes such as Funny, Bold, Emotional, Aesthetic, Attitude, or Gen-Z

Team **Hustle** -- Fareed Amir, Laiba Akram
