### FRA Atlas
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fra-atlas-ae11) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/dhananjaysaini44/Improved-fra) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://improved-fra.onrender.com/health) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WlWxdbFxCfI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknovate--7.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknovate07.devfolio.co)

> FRA Atlas and Web GIS System (Drishti)

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FRA Atlas (Drishti) is a digital platform that helps people and officials manage Forest Rights Act (FRA) land claims in a more organized, transparent, and map-based way. In simple terms, it is a system where a claim can be submitted, checked, reviewed, and tracked from start to finish, instead of being handled only through scattered paper files.
This project is mainly for three groups. First, it helps claimants or field users who need to submit land rights claims with documents and location details. Second, it supports government or administrative reviewers (such as Tehsildars/Patwari) who verify claims, detect conflicts, and approve or reject submissions. Third, it helps supervisors (officers) and policy teams who need dashboards, trends, and audit records to understand what is happening across regions.
The platform works through a web app connected to a backend and a document-analysis service. A user fills in claim details such as claimant name, village, district, and state. They can upload supporting documents (for example PDFs or images) and define the land area on a map, either by drawing boundaries or selecting relevant local land references like Khasra-linked parcels. Once submitted, the claim is saved in the system and assigned a status such as pending, approved, or rejected.
A key part of the project is geospatial intelligence. Claims are not treated as text only; they are tied to map geometry (polygons). The system checks whether a new claim overlaps with existing claims, whether location details appear consistent, and whether there are warning signals that require manual review. This helps reduce accidental duplicates and identify land conflicts earlier.
Another key part is document intelligence. A Python OCR/model pipeline reads uploaded documents, extracts useful fields, and generates structured outputs and confidence signals. These outputs are then attached to the claim so reviewers do not have to start from scratch for every file. Importantly, human admins still make final decisions; the model is used as decision support, not a replacement for officials.
For governance and trust, the project also keeps strong audit visibility. Important actions such as approvals or rejections are logged, and selected events can be anchored to Algorand so records are tamper-evident. This improves accountability and creates a verifiable history of decisions.
Overall, FRA Atlas is a practical bridge between people, land records, maps, and administration. It reduces manual friction, improves traceability, and gives reviewers clearer evidence before making decisions. In real-world terms, it is meant to make FRA claim processing faster, fairer, and easier to monitor at scale while still respecting local land systems and human review workflows.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0b168a4f66314fedbed84586c883a426/752c0422-e5bc-4e0c-aa00-6a68dd41f410.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Multi-service integration was hard because frontend, backend, and Python OCR/pipeline had to stay in sync. We had to handle failures gracefully so claim submission never broke even when model services failed.

2. Geospatial validation was challenging due to inconsistent polygon inputs (drawn, GPS, Khasra-linked). Small geometry differences could affect overlap/conflict detection and required careful normalization.

3. Blockchain anchoring added trust but also operational complexity. We made Algorand integration non-blocking so approvals/rejections continue even if anchoring temporarily fails using algosdk.

4. Frequent parallel development caused merge conflicts and regression risk. We needed strict merge resolution and post-merge verification to avoid feature or code loss.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0b168a4f66314fedbed84586c883a426/04306405-e8e6-424d-8eec-ae02cc87dcbc.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0b168a4f66314fedbed84586c883a426/e1318a44-c544-4897-b33e-76a637af48fc.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/0b168a4f66314fedbed84586c883a426/05dbd61e-f6b7-4a0e-9c84-9959f03d3fa5.png)

**Algorand**

This project uses Algorand as an integrity layer for key claim decisions.
When an admin approves or rejects a claim, the backend creates a structured decision payload. It generates a deterministic local hash from that payload. That hash is anchored on Algorand, and the transaction ID is returned.
Both the local hash and Algorand transaction ID are stored in audit_ledger.
The event is also written to system logs for operational traceability. Only proof data (hash), not full documents, is sent on-chain. This keeps sensitive claim data private while enabling verification.
If Algorand anchoring fails, the claim workflow still continues gracefully. The failure is logged so no action is silently lost. Auditors can later recompute the hash and match it with the on-chain record.
So Algorand provides tamper-evident trust without replacing the main database.

Face recognition matching against government databases
Real-time case status tracking
Police Portal

> "Because Every Ride Deserves a Safe Return.”

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Internet of Things (IoT)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Internet%20of%20Things%20(IoT)-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

HelmoSafe not only responds to accidents but acts proactively to enhance rider safety before situations turn critical. Many two-wheeler riders, especially on analog bikes, lack access to smart safety systems that can assist them in real-time.

How It Helps:
*Provides proactive safety support by continuously monitoring and staying ready for emergencies
*Enables instant SOS alerts and calls without requiring rider intervention
*Works seamlessly with traditional bikes, making safety accessible to a larger population
*Reduces panic and response time by ensuring help is triggered immediately.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major real-world challenge was making HelmoSafe compatible with traditional (analog) bikes. Most bikes don’t have digital systems or easy access to signals like ignition status, so integrating the system wasn’t straightforward.

I also faced difficulty in figuring out how to detect vehicle state and trigger safety features without modifying the bike’s core wiring too much. Ensuring the system stays affordable, non-invasive, and easy to install was a big hurdle.

HOW I SOLVED IT?

I approached this by:
*Using a simple DC motor simulation to represent ignition instead of relying on complex bike electronics
*Designing the system to be independent of advanced sensors, so it can work on basic bikes..
*Keeping wiring minimal and focusing on external add-on components.

### SpeakTech
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/speaktech-ea1a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/twinkle1403/SpeakTeach.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/jClDWfxupdA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknovate--7.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknovate07.devfolio.co)

> Every Word, Better Than Before

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves:**

Many individuals face speech challenges such as stuttering, lisp, and lack of fluency. Access to professional speech therapy is often limited due to high costs, lack of availability, and the need for frequent in-person sessions. Additionally, users do not receive continuous, real-time feedback, which makes consistent improvement difficult.

As a result, speech practice becomes irregular, unguided, and less effective.

**How People Can Use It:**

SpeakTech AI is a web-based platform that allows users to practice and improve their speech independently using AI-driven feedback.

**Users can:**

1. Practice speaking in real time using voice input
2. Receive instant accuracy analysis of their speech
3. Identify pronunciation errors, repeated words, and fluency issues
4. Get personalized suggestions and targeted practice drills
5. Complete structured worksheets for guided learning
6. Track their progress over time using performance analytics

**How It Improves Existing Solutions:**

SpeakTech AI simplifies and enhances speech therapy by:

1. Providing instant feedback instead of delayed evaluation
2. Eliminating the need for constant therapist supervision
3. Making speech practice accessible anytime and anywhere
4. Offering a structured and measurable improvement process
5. Adapting suggestions based on user performance

**Impact :**

SpeakTech AI makes speech improvement more accessible, consistent, and data-driven. It enables users to practice privately, build confidence, and work on their weaknesses through continuous feedback and personalized guidance.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I Ran Into:**

1.Browser compatibility issues with speech recognition:

The Web Speech API behaved inconsistently across browsers and sometimes stopped capturing input. I handled this by adding error handling, restarting recognition automatically, and guiding users to supported browsers.

2.Inaccurate speech analysis using basic comparison:

Simple string matching failed to handle partial matches and pronunciation variations. I improved this by implementing a word-level accuracy system using tokenization and Levenshtein distance.

3.Detecting repeated words and speech patterns:

Identifying stuttering and repeated words in real-time was challenging. I solved this by building a repetition detection logic that tracks word frequency and highlights problem words.

### Build Mate
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/build-mate-30f7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Mr-animesh/Build-Mate) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/rMztDUf6c0Y) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknovate--7.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknovate07.devfolio.co)

> Build together , Stay Local

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The project, BuildMate (also referred to as the SkillSwap Platform), is an AI-driven ecosystem designed to bridge the gap between technical talent, project collaboration, and recruitment. It moves beyond traditional resume-based matching by leveraging raw data from public contributions.

The Problem It Solves
**The Collaboration Discovery Gap:** Many talented developers have great ideas or specific skills (like UI design) but lack the counterpart (like Backend architecture) to ship a real product. Finding someone with the right "DNA" (tech stack + complexity level) within the same city/university is a manual, inefficient process.
Inefficient Technical Sourcing: Large-scale recruiting relies on keyword matching. This ignores the quality and difficulty of the code. Manually auditing GitHub repositories is too time-consuming for recruiters at scale.

What People Use It For
For Developers & Builders:
Skill Swapping: A developer can "trade" their expertise (e.g., Python backend) for another's (e.g., React frontend) to build and ship projects together without monetary exchange.
Automatic Portfolio Generation: By simply providing a GitHub URL, the platform uses AI (GPT-4o-mini) to summarize their best work, highlight their tech stack, and assign a complexity score to their repositories.
Local Networking: Users can filter "builders" by city (Delhi, Bangalore, Mumbai, etc.) to assemble in-person teams for hackathons or startups.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The Multi-Stage AI Profile Evaluation Pipeline
The Challenge: Transforming a raw GitHub URL into a structured technical "DNA" report was not a single step. We had to:

Fetch raw stats (stars, forks, languages) via the GitHub REST API.
Pass these technical signals to an LLM (GPT-4o-mini).
Generate a narrative summary and a quantitative Difficulty Score (1–50).
The Hurdle: LLMs can be inconsistent. Sometimes they would return markdown code blocks, and other times they would miss critical tags, breaking our backend's ability to save the data to MongoDB.

2. Semantic Matchmaking (Keywords + Geo-Location)
The Challenge: A recruiter might search for a "React engineer in Mumbai who understands Web3." Traditional database queries (like find({ location: 'Mumbai', skills: 'React' })) are too rigid. If a developer wrote "Bombay" or "Lower Parel" instead of "Mumbai," or "Solidity" instead of "Web3," the recruiter would get zero results.

The Hurdle: How do we match a "Mission Description" (natural language) against a "User Profile" (structured data) while also respecting a strict geographic constraint?

The Solution: I built a Hybrid Matchmaking Engine:

Geographic Tokenization: Location strings are normalized into "tokens" (e.g., "New York" and "NYC" both map to the same region).
LLM-Augmented Search: For the technical side, the system doesn't just look for exact keywords. It uses the AI-generated Project Summary and Keywords (like "scalable APIs," "low-latency") to find "Semantic Overlap." This means if a developer built a high-performance C++ engine, they can be matched with a mission asking for "System optimization," even if the word wasn't in their bio.
3. Handling GitHub API Rate Limits & Normalization
The Challenge: GitHub's API is strict. If many users register at once, our backend's IP address could be temporarily banned. Furthermore, users provide GitHub URLs in many formats (e.g., github.com/user, https://github.com/user/, git@github.com:user).

The Hurdle: Inconsistent data entry and API bottlenecks prevented us from creating a "Single Source of Truth."

### Assistly
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/assistly-15f9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AnubhavScripts/Hacknovate) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://assistly-iota.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknovate--7.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknovate07.devfolio.co)

> Turn chats into conversions with AI

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Compass](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Compass-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Businesses today handle customer interactions across multiple channels like WhatsApp, email, and websites. These conversations are often unstructured, scattered, and difficult to manage efficiently.

As a result:

Important customer queries are delayed or missed
High-intent leads are not identified in time
Teams manually respond to repetitive messages
There is no clear visibility into customer intent or journey

In sectors like finance (loans, credit) and e-commerce, this leads to lost conversions, poor customer experience, and inefficient operations.

Assistly addresses this problem by transforming raw conversations into structured, actionable insights. It uses AI to understand user intent, classify leads (HOT/WARM/COLD), and automate intelligent responses, enabling businesses to respond faster, prioritize better, and convert more effectively.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Handling Real-Time WhatsApp Communication

Integrating WhatsApp via Twilio required managing webhooks, message formats, and validation. Initial issues included unreliable message handling and sandbox limitations.
Solution: Implemented secure webhook validation, standardized message processing, and added fallback/mock handling for development.

2. AI Misclassification of Short Messages

Messages like “yes”, “ok”, and “hmm” were incorrectly classified as invalid, breaking conversation flow.
Solution: Improved AI prompts and added backend logic to treat such inputs as conversation continuations based on context.

3. Maintaining Conversation Context

Early responses were stateless, causing repetitive or irrelevant replies.
Solution: Introduced conversation history tracking and passed recent messages to the AI, along with generating summaries for better context retention.

4. Accurate Lead Classification

Determining whether a user is a HOT, WARM, or COLD lead based on incomplete or vague inputs was challenging.
Solution: Combined AI-based intent detection with rule-based scoring and entity extraction (salary, loan amount, urgency) to improve accuracy.

5. Making Conversations Human-Like

Initial responses felt generic and robotic.
Solution: Built a follow-up engine to ask relevant next questions, avoided repetition using memory, and personalized replies using extracted user data.

6. Data Modeling for Conversations

Storing logs per message made it hard to understand overall user intent.
Solution: Introduced a conversation-level model to store summaries, lead status, and progression, improving analytics and dashboard clarity.

7. Merging Distributed Codebases

Frontend and backend were developed across multiple branches, leading to large conflicts and structural inconsistencies.
Solution: Replaced the frontend completely and merged backend components selectively to preserve functionality and avoid breaking changes.

8. Dependency Conflicts

Different environments had mismatched dependencies, especially in backend configurations.
Solution: Carefully merged package.json files and regenerated lock files to ensure stability and compatibility.

9. Supporting Multiple Business Flows

The system initially treated all interactions as customer support, failing to handle finance-specific queries like loans.
Solution: Introduced dynamic flow switching (sales vs support) with context-aware AI prompts.

### Mesh Alert
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/mesh-alert-8243) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/CKhurana13/MeshAlert) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknovate--7.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknovate07.devfolio.co)

> Mesh Alert - No Internet. No Problem.

![Android Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20Studio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bluetooth Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bluetooth%20Module-333333?style=flat-square) ![Leaflet.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Leaflet.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

During natural disasters, earthquakes, floods, or civil emergencies, cellular networks and internet infrastructure collapse precisely when communication is most critical. MeshRelay solves this by turning every Android phone into a self-sufficient relay node — no towers, no internet, no central server required.Using Bluetooth Low Energy advertising packets, the app creates a spontaneous peer-to-peer mesh network. Messages fragment across BLE payloads, hop between nearby devices, and self-reassemble — extending range far beyond a single device's Bluetooth radius through cooperative relay. Anyone in the mesh can broadcast SOS distress signals with live GPS coordinates, request emergency resources (water, food, medical aid, shelter), or send free-text messages up to 160 characters — all of which propagate outward through every phone in range. A live Leaflet map plots every node that has broadcast location data, giving rescuers and survivors a real-time spatial picture of who is where.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. BLE payload size constraints were the biggest hurdle. Android's BLE advertiser caps manufacturer-specific data at roughly 26 bytes per packet. Fitting a meaningful message into that meant designing a custom 6-byte fragmentation header (type, 3-byte message ID, chunk index, total chunks) with 20-byte data payloads per chunk — and writing a reassembly buffer on the receiver side that waits for all chunks before delivering the message. Getting chunk ordering, deduplication, and partial-fragment cleanup right without a connection-oriented channel took several iterations.

2. Relay storm prevention was equally tricky. A naive mesh re-broadcasts every received message immediately, causing exponential packet storms that saturate the BLE medium within seconds. The solution was a randomised relay delay (200–600 ms jitter) combined with a seen-IDs set that gates both reception and re-transmission, ensuring each unique message ID is forwarded at most once per node.

3. Concurrent advertise/scan on the same adapter proved unreliable on many chipsets — Android does not guarantee simultaneous advertising and scanning. The workaround was a serialised send queue that stops the current advertiser, transmits a chunk for 400 ms, then resumes scanning in the gaps, trading some throughput for compatibility across devices.

4. GPS cold-start latency meant the SOS button could fire before a fix was acquired. This was handled by falling back to "NO_GPS" in the SOS payload and requesting both GPS and Network providers in parallel, so a coarse network fix populates the map while the precise satellite fix catches up.

### SightSync
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sightsync-bdb7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/mishti-guptaa/SightSyncProject) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknovate--7.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknovate07.devfolio.co)

> AI that sees, so you don't have to.

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![YOLOv8](https://img.shields.io/badge/YOLOv8-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

We propose an AI-powered system that helps visually impaired users detect objects and identify currency in real time. Using a camera, the system captures surroundings and processes them with a trained model (like YOLO) to recognize objects and currency notes. The detected information is instantly converted into voice feedback (e.g., “Chair ahead” or “₹500 note detected”).

This solution is designed as a mobile app, ensuring accessibility, fast response, and improved independence for users in daily life.

**Challenges we ran into**

•	Dataset availability: Limited and inconsistent datasets for Indian currency and real-world object scenarios.
	•	Accuracy issues: Difficulty in detecting objects and currency under poor lighting, blur, or occlusion.
	•	Real-time performance: Balancing speed and accuracy for smooth, low-latency detection.
	•	Model optimization: Making the model lightweight enough to run on mobile devices.
	•	Voice feedback timing: Ensuring audio output is clear, timely, and not overwhelming for the user.
	•	Similar object confusion: Distinguishing between visually similar objects or currency notes.

### Beacon
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/beacon-41f2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/team-zerolatency/beacon/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackMol%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackmol-7.devfolio.co)

> When Networks Fail, We Don’t

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

** The Impact of BEACON: Redefining Disaster Communication**

In a disaster, the "Golden Hour" is the window where medical intervention has the highest chance of preventing death. BEACON ensures that even when the world goes offline, the lifeline stays connected
.
**1. Primary Use Cases: Who uses it and why?**
For Trapped Survivors:
The "One-Tap" Lifeline: In high-stress situations (earthquakes, floods), users don't have time to navigate complex menus. A single tap broadcasts their GPS coordinates, battery level, and medical status to everyone nearby.
Silent Hailing: If a survivor is trapped and needs to stay quiet (e.g., in a structural collapse or security threat), they can signal for help without making a sound.
For First Responders & NGOs:
Precision Rescue: Instead of searching broad zones, rescue teams see a Heatmap of SOS signals on the Next.js Dashboard. This allows them to prioritize high-density casualty areas.
Safe Navigation: Rescuers can mark "Danger Zones" (e.g., a broken bridge) on the map, which then propagates back through the mesh to warn other survivors.
For Displaced Families:
The "I am Safe" Broadcast: Even without a signal, a user can broadcast a "Safe" status. When any phone in the mesh eventually hits a 4G/Wi-Fi zone, that status is uploaded, notifying worried family members via the web portal.

**2. How BEACON Improves Existing Tasks**
Existing Task	Traditional Method (The Old Way)	With BEACON (The New Way)
Sending an SOS	Repeatedly dialing emergency numbers hoping for a signal.	Automatic Propagation: The phone keeps "shouting" via Bluetooth until a neighbor hears it.
Location Tracking	Rescuers guess location based on last known cell tower ping.	Real-Time GPS: Precise coordinates are hopped through the mesh to the dashboard.
Information Flow	Word-of-mouth or radio (limited range/expensive).	Digital Mesh: High-speed data transfer across a decentralized network of smartphones.
Helping Non-Tech Users	Feature phone users are completely cut off.	SMS Fallback: Uses Twilio to bridge the gap between mesh signals and basic GSM.

**3. Safety & Efficiency Benefits**
 Eliminating "Communication Black Holes"
Traditional apps are "Cloud-First." If the Cloud is unreachable, the app is a brick. BEACON is "Edge-First," meaning the intelligence lives on the device. This eliminates the silence that usually follows a infrastructure collapse.
 Reducing Search Time
In floods or cyclones, visibility is low. By providing rescuers with a Mapbox-powered offline visualization, BEACON turns a "Search and Rescue" operation into a "Locate and Extract" operation—saving hours of critical time.
Power-Aware Resilience
Unlike GPS-heavy apps that drain battery, BEACON uses Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). It is designed to stay active for days, not hours, ensuring the survivor's phone doesn't die before help arrives.

**4. The "Network Effect" Safety Net**
The unique strength of BEACON is that the more people use it, the safer everyone becomes.
In a crowded city, the mesh is dense and near-instant.
In rural areas, even a single IoT Beacon Node (Future Scope) at a community center acts as a permanent "Digital Lighthouse" for miles.

**Challenges we ran into**

** Challenges I Ran Into**
Building a decentralized communication system in a weekend came with significant technical hurdles. Here is how we navigated the most difficult parts of the build:

**1. The "Native" Wall: Integrating Google Nearby with Expo**
The Hurdle: We initially started with a standard Expo "Managed" workflow. However, we quickly realized that the Google Nearby Connections API requires deep access to native Android/iOS Bluetooth and Wi-Fi drivers, which are not available in the standard Expo Go app.
The Fix: We had to pivot to Expo Development Builds (using npx expo prebuild). This allowed us to write custom Native Modules and configure the AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist with the necessary high-level permissions (Fine Location, Bluetooth Advertise, etc.) while still keeping the speed of React Native development.

**2. The "Hop" Logic: Moving beyond P2P to a Mesh**
The Hurdle: Google Nearby Connections is traditionally Peer-to-Peer (P2P). If Phone A connects to Phone B, and Phone B connects to Phone C, Phone A cannot "see" Phone C by default. Our goal was a true mesh where the SOS could travel across multiple "hops."
The Fix: We implemented a "Store-and-Forward" Relay Logic. We designed a packet structure that includes a Unique_SOS_ID. When a device receives a payload, it checks its local cache. If the ID is new, it stores it and immediately re-broadcasts it to all other connected neighbors. This effectively turned a simple P2P connection into a propagating mesh.

**3. Battery vs. Persistence: Staying Alive in the Background**
The Hurdle: Modern mobile operating systems (especially Android 12+ and iOS) are aggressive at killing background apps to save battery. For a disaster app, if the app is killed, the mesh node dies, breaking the chain for everyone else.
The Fix: We implemented Android Foreground Services with a persistent notification. This signals to the OS that the app is performing a critical life-safety task, preventing it from being put into "Deep Sleep." We also optimized the scanning interval—using a "Heartbeat" scan every 30 seconds rather than a constant drain—to balance resilience with battery life.

**4. The Data Bottleneck: Handling BLE MTU Limits**
The Hurdle: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) has a very small Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU). We initially tried to send a large JSON object containing user names, detailed coordinates, and timestamps, but the packets were frequently dropped or truncated.
The Fix: We stripped the data down to a Compact Byte Array. We mapped specific codes to medical statuses (e.g., 01 = Medical, 02 = Fire) and used Unix timestamps to keep the payload under the 256-byte limit. This ensured 99% delivery success across the mesh.

**5. The "Connectivity Vacuum": Offline-First Syncing**
The Hurdle: Managing the transition from "Fully Offline" to "Cloud Connected" was tricky. We needed to ensure that when a node finally hit a Wi-Fi zone, it didn't just upload its own data, but all the cached SOS signals it had picked up from others.
The Fix: We utilized Supabase with a "Queue Processing" logic. All incoming mesh signals are stored in a local SQLite database first. We created a "Network Listener" that triggers as soon as an internet handshake is detected, batch-uploading the entire local queue to the NGO Dashboard in a single transaction.

### DigiRakshak
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/digirakshak-10a0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackMol%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackmol-7.devfolio.co)

> From detection to prevention

![Expo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Expo-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Java](https://img.shields.io/badge/Java-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Fraud today is no longer obvious. Messages look like they are coming from banks, delivery services, or trusted platforms. They create urgency and pressure users to act quickly, often leading to people clicking malicious links or sharing sensitive information.

The core issue is not just detection, it is timing.

Most existing solutions either label spam at a basic level or react after the fraud has already happened. There is no system that actively helps the user at the exact moment they are making a risky decision.

DigiRakshak addresses this gap by shifting the focus from detection to prevention.

Instead of only classifying messages, the system analyzes SMS and URLs in real time using on device intelligence. It also uses pattern based threat intelligence inspired by large scale systems to recognize evolving fraud patterns.

Most importantly, it explains the risk clearly to the user, so they understand why something is dangerous before taking action.

The goal is simple. Help users make safer decisions in real time and stop fraud before it happens.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. **Architecture redesign after mentor feedback**
   During the mentor round, we studied how Bharti Airtel approaches fraud detection at scale. This led us to realize that our initial backend heavy design was limited. We had to redesign the system into a more edge driven and distributed architecture, which required significant changes in data flow and system structure.

2. **Data imbalance in machine learning models**
   Fraud datasets are highly imbalanced, with very few malicious samples compared to normal data. This affected model performance and required careful handling through preprocessing and tuning to avoid biased predictions.

3. **Real time message access limitations**
   Accessing messages in real time, especially from platforms like WhatsApp, was not feasible due to encryption and platform restrictions. This forced us to shift our focus toward SMS, URLs, and pattern based detection instead of relying on inaccessible data sources.

**Main Track: The Deepforge Arena**

### WhereIsMyBus
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/whereismybus-84be) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/who-princee/WhereIsMyBus) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackMol%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackmol-7.devfolio.co)

> Because Guessing is Outdated!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase Cloud Messaging](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase%20Cloud%20Messaging-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Public buses are the primary mode of public transport
in many Indian cities, carrying 40–60% of urban
public transport passengers. However, the system
often lacks real time information and reliable arrival
updates, making commuting inefficient and
unpredictable. Without GPS based tracking or
accurate arrival estimates, passengers are forced to
rely on uncertain schedules, while parents have no
visibility into the safety and location of school buses.
No Live Tracking: Many bus services still lack real time
tracking, leaving commuters unaware of bus locations and
schedules.
Unpredictable Arrivals: Around 28% of commuters report
delays and irregular bus timings as a major problem in public
transport systems.
Limited Bus Safety: Without monitoring systems, parents
cannot track school buses or know their children’s exact
commute status.
Reduced Public Transport Usage: 37% of commuters avoid
public transport due to overcrowding and poor service
reliability, showing declining trust in the system

**Challenges we ran into**

​1. The "Ghost Bus" Problem (Data Accuracy)
​The biggest challenge is syncing Static Data (schedules) with Real-time Data (GPS).
​GTFS-Realtime Issues: Most cities use the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS). Often, the real-time feed won't match the static schedule IDs. If a bus's trip_id in the live feed doesn't exist in your schedule database, the app won't know which route to show, creating a "ghost bus."
​GPS Drift & Urban Canyons: In cities with tall buildings, GPS signals bounce (multipath interference). This makes a bus appear to be driving through buildings or on a parallel street, which triggers false "arrived at stop" notifications.  
​2. Latency & Refresh Rates
​The 30-Second Gap: Most public feeds only update every 15–30 seconds. If a user is standing at a stop and the bus is 10 seconds away, but your app says it's 40 seconds away because of a lag in the feed, they might give up and walk away just as the bus pulls up.
​Server Strain: Real-time tracking requires constant "polling" (asking the server for updates). If you have 10,000 users all asking for updates every 5 seconds, your server costs and battery drain on the users' phones will skyrocket.
​3. The "Last Mile" of Human Error
​Driver Behavior: Drivers sometimes forget to log into their GPS consoles or accidentally log into the wrong route. Your app might show Bus A on Route 10, but it’s actually running Route 12.
​Detours & Traffic: Standard ETA algorithms often fail to account for sudden accidents or temporary construction detours that aren't updated in the official transit feed.

### SafeRoute
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/saferoute-9705) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Chandragupta555/SafeRoute.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackMol%207.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackmol-7.devfolio.co)

> Women Safety Navigator

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every navigation app tells you the fastest route. None tells you the safest one.

Women in Indian cities face three problems no app is solving today:

Blind Routing — Google Maps routes through dark alleys and isolated stretches at midnight. Speed is prioritized, safety is ignored.

No Feedback Loop — Women report unsafe areas but those reports never influence future navigation. The data goes nowhere.

Dead Zone Failure — Every existing safety app is 100% internet-dependent. They fail exactly when and where they're needed most.

SafeRoute solves all three — safety-first routing, a community feedback loop that makes the map smarter over time, and an offline SOS fallback that never goes silent.

**Challenges we ran into**

Cold Start Problem — A blank map on Day 1 means no users, and no users means no data. Solved by pre-seeding 150 real incidents across Chandigarh sectors using NCRB Crime Statistics 2022.

Offline SOS — Safety apps are useless in network dead zones. We built local GPS caching every 30 seconds with automatic SMS fallback via Fast2SMS — no internet required.

Honest Scoring Model — Mentor feedback pushed us to replace hardcoded logic with a proper 5-parameter weighted scoring system covering historical crime, recent reports, time-of-day risk, community feedback, and path conditions.

Free Stack Navigation — Replicating Google Maps-style live navigation with route progress, camera tracking, and live safety score updates — entirely on Leaflet, OSRM, and OpenStreetMap with zero paid APIs.

PWA Architecture — Building an installable offline-first PWA with service workers, real-time Socket.io, and a mobile-first UI that works seamlessly across both online and offline states.

**Main Track: The Deepforge Arena**

SafeRoute addresses one of the most underserved problems in civic tech — women's safety in urban navigation. It goes beyond a basic hackathon project by combining a multi-parameter weighted safety scoring engine, real-time live navigation, community-driven data collection, offline SMS fallback architecture, and a clear B2B monetization model targeting cab operators, corporates, and universities. The technical depth — custom routing on a fully free stack, PWA offline-first architecture, Socket.io real-time tracking, and a feedback loop designed to evolve into full ML at scale — makes it a production-viable product, not just a prototype. SafeRoute competes in the main track because it is built to solve a real problem at real scale.

**Fresher’s Track: The Rising Lanterns**

Every member of our team is participating in their first hackathon. Coming in with no prior hackathon experience, we built a full-stack PWA from scratch in 30 hours — a React frontend, Node/Express backend, MongoDB database, real-time Socket.io tracking, live Leaflet navigation, and an SMS emergency alert system. We made mistakes, debugged at 3am, rewrote our scoring engine after mentor feedback mid-hackathon, and kept building. SafeRoute represents exactly what the freshers track stands for — first-timers who didn't play it safe, took on a hard problem, and shipped something real.

### Sustainify
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/sustainify-88c8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/shreyashree0207/devshouse) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/a9XSdtcgRzw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DevsHouse%20'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devshouse26.devfolio.co)

> Donate with Proof , Give with Purpose

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sustainify addresses a fundamental trust gap in charitable donations. When someone donates money to an NGO, they have no way of knowing whether their contribution actually reached the intended cause or was used as promised.

Traditional donation platforms accept any image or update from NGOs without verification. There is no accountability layer, no way to distinguish genuine NGOs from fraudulent ones, and no proof that milestones are actually being completed.

Sustainify solves this by combining AI-powered image verification with real-time milestone tracking. When an NGO uploads a proof image, our system automatically analyzes whether the image is a real photograph taken at an actual location, an AI generated image, or a stock photo downloaded from the internet. It also checks whether the image actually matches what the NGO claims to have done. This makes it extremely difficult for NGOs to fake their progress reports.

Donors can see a live transparency score for every NGO, calculated from their verified proof uploads, milestone completion rate, and donor retention. They also receive a specific impact message after donating that tells them exactly what their contribution will fund.

For NGOs, the platform creates an incentive to be transparent because their visibility and trust score depends on uploading genuine verified proof. Blacklisted or underperforming NGOs are flagged automatically.

The platform is useful for anyone who wants to donate to a cause but has hesitated because they do not trust where their money goes. It is also useful for corporates fulfilling CSR obligations who need documented proof of impact, and for government bodies that want to monitor NGO activity against funded milestones.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our biggest challenge was the image verification system returning inconsistent output formats, which broke our parsing logic. We handled this by adding strict output formatting and fallback responses.

Database schema issues were frequent since our features kept evolving mid-build, causing missing column errors. We fixed these on the go using ALTER TABLE statements.

We also ran into foreign key violations when inserting related data because we were using placeholder IDs instead of real database values. Once we identified the pattern we always fetched real IDs first before any insert.

Finally CORS errors blocked our frontend from talking to the backend until we added the correct middleware configuration

**Open Innovation**

Sustainify fits Open Innovation because it tackles a systemic problem across multiple sectors simultaneously. Fake NGOs, misallocated funds, and unverified impact reports are problems that affect donors, government bodies, and society equally. Our solution bridges three communities into one accountable platform.

For donors, it provides complete visibility into where their money goes, with real time milestone tracking and verified proof before and after every activity.

For NGOs, it creates a structured accountability system where transparency directly builds donor trust and unlocks government funding points through verified milestone completion.

For government bodies, it provides a monitoring layer where NGO activity, proof uploads, and fund utilization are all tracked and auditable in one place. Suspicious or blacklisted NGOs are flagged automatically.

Every uploaded proof image undergoes a four stage verification pipeline. First it checks authenticity to determine if the image is real or fabricated. Then it verifies relevance by checking if the image actually matches what the NGO claims to have done. Next it analyzes geolocation to confirm the activity happened in the correct region. Finally it computes a trust score based on all three layers combined. Perceptual hashing also generates a digital fingerprint of every image to instantly detect duplicate fraud across different NGOs.

Built with Next.js and Tailwind CSS on the frontend, FastAPI on the backend, and Supabase for database, authentication, and storage. Role based access ensures donors, NGO admins, and government monitors each see only what is relevant to them.

What makes it innovative is that instead of treating donation platforms as simple payment gateways, we built a full accountability layer serving three distinct communities simultaneously, making fraud extremely difficult without adding complexity for any of them.

> See through walls using wi-fi

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP-32 WiFi Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP--32%20WiFi%20Module-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Where it can be used-
· Occupancy‑Based Automation – Automatically turn off lights/HVAC when a room is empty, even if the sensor is in another room. Works through walls, so you can cover multiple rooms with fewer devices.
· Fall Detection – Detect sudden motion or lack of movement in a bedroom or bathroom without installing cameras (privacy‑preserving). Alert caregivers immediately.
· Wandering Prevention – Monitor if a person with dementia leaves a safe zone (e.g., exits the living room into the hallway) and send a notification
· Search & Rescue – First responders can quickly determine if a room contains moving victims before entering, reducing risk in hostage situations, fires, or collapsed structures.
· Through‑Wall Awareness – Police can assess if a suspect is moving behind a closed door, allowing safer tactical decisions..
· Restroom Occupancy – Detect if a restroom stall is occupied through the wall—useful in airports, malls, or offices.
· Industrial Safety – Detect personnel movement in hazardous areas without requiring them to wear tracking devices.

How exactly is better than any existing solutions-
Your Wi-ESPectre project solves three critical problems that existing technologies fail to address:

---

1. The “Flash Effect” – Seeing Through Walls

Current smart home sensors (PIR, cameras) cannot detect motion through walls. Military radar can, but it’s expensive and bulky. Your solution uses Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) and Moving Variance Segmentation (MVS) to cancel the overwhelming wall reflection (the “flash”) and isolate human motion—all with a ESP32.

2. Privacy vs. Security Trade-off

Cameras and wearables invade privacy; thermal imagers are blocked by glass and walls. Your system detects motion passively using existing Wi-Fi signals—no images, no wearables, just radio wave analysis. It respects privacy while providing real‑time awareness.

3. Inaccessible Through‑Wall Sensing

Traditional through‑wall radar costs lakhs and crores and requires licenses. Your solution makes through‑wall motion detection affordable, compact, and accessible to homeowners, first responders, and small businesses—democratizing a technology previously reserved for the military.

**Challenges we ran into**

The Flash Effect is the biggest challenge in through‑wall motion detection.
When a Wi‑Fi signal hits a wall:
· Most of the signal reflects off the wall (like a mirror)
· Only a tiny fraction passes through, reflects off a person, and returns
The wall’s reflection is 10,000–100,000 times stronger than the person’s reflection. This is the Flash Effect—the wall’s echo “flashes” and overwhelms the receiver, making the person’s signal invisible.
Analogy: Camera Flash & Mirror

Imagine taking a photo of a person standing in front of a large mirror with your camera flash on. The mirror reflects almost all the flash back into the camera, leaving the person completely washed out. The wall acts just like that mirror.

 How We Solved It
We used baseline subtraction:

· First, we recorded the Wi‑Fi signal when the room was empty (only the wall’s reflection).
· Then, we continuously subtracted this “static” signal from new readings.
· What remains is only the changes caused by motion—the person’s faint reflection is revealed.

This allows our ESP32 to “see” through walls, detecting movement without expensive radar.

**IoT & Smart Devices**

The Wi-ESPectre project transforms a standard Wi‑Fi chip into a smart, privacy‑aware motion sensor that integrates seamlessly into the IoT ecosystem. It’s a perfect example of how IoT devices can leverage existing infrastructure (Wi‑Fi) to provide new, valuable services – making homes safer, more efficient, and responsive without compromising privacy.

**The problem it solves**

Modern digital interfaces assume hands + precise control, making them difficult or impossible to use for:

People with motor disabilities
Users in constrained environments (e.g., surgery rooms, labs)
Situations where hands are occupied

This project introduces a gaze-based interaction system that allows users to control UI elements using only their eyes.

What people can use it for:
Accessibility: Enable hands-free interaction for physically challenged users
Productivity: Navigate dashboards, apps, or systems without switching input modes
Specialized environments: Use computers in sterile or restricted setups

How it improves existing systems:
Enables a more natural, intent-driven interface using gaze + dwell
Easy Integration
Scalable and Modular System

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Inconsistent Eye Tracking (especially vertical movement)
The model tracked left-right well but struggled with up-down accuracy
Root cause: poor calibration + limited training data variation

Solution:
Implemented a calibration UI with multiple screen points to train the model dynamically per user.

2. False Positives in Click (accidental triggers)
Buttons were activating just by passing gaze over them

Solution:
Added a dwell-time mechanism:

Action only triggers if gaze stays on element for a threshold duration
Combined with “lock + confirm” logic to prevent accidental execution

3. Model Drift Over Time
Accuracy degraded after continuous use

Solution:
Periodic recalibration prompts
Lightweight real-time correction using recent gaze data

4. Mac → Windows Project Corruption
ZIP transfer created __MACOSX junk folders
Broke project structure and confused tooling

Solution:
Cleaned directory structure
Re-initialized environment and dependencies

**Open Innovation**

This project aligns strongly with Open Innovation by:
1. Leveraging Open Technologies - Built on open-source tools like GazeCloud.js and it encourages extensibility and community-driven improvements. 

2. Enabling Accessibility for All
Not locked to proprietary hardware and can run on standard webcams that lowers entry barrier

3. Designed for Integration for it can plug into anything - 
Web apps, Assistive tech platforms, Smart environments

4. Encouraging Future Contributions
The modular architecture allows : 
Better ML models, Improved calibration systems, Cross-device compatibility

> "Fairness in motion ,equity in action"

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AEQUITAS analyzes multiple workload factors such as the number of packages, package weight, travel distance, and physical effort like stairs or apartment deliveries. It calculates a normalized difficulty score for each delivery route and uses a load-balancing algorithm to distribute routes fairly among drivers. The system integrates with Google Maps to visually display routes, highlight difficulty zones, and provide transparent explanations for assignments. By prioritizing fairness instead of only speed and cost, AEQUITAS aims to reduce driver fatigue, improve safety, increase transparency, and support sustainable logistics operations.

**Challenges we ran into**

Here are the challenges faced during AEQUITAS development in paragraph form:
One of the earliest challenges was the package assignment pipeline finding zero drivers, which turned out to be because newly registered drivers never had their available_dates field populated — this required a one-time fix script to patch all existing driver records in MongoDB.
The driver dashboard showing only one package was a subtle but critical bug — the code used find_one() instead of find() when querying assignments, meaning only the first subarea cluster was ever returned. Since each subarea is stored as a separate assignment document, drivers with multiple areas assigned to them could only see a fraction of their workload.
Package status updates failing with "Failed to update" happened because the PATCH route tried to convert the package ID to a MongoDB ObjectId, but packages uploaded via CSV have string IDs like PKG001 — not valid ObjectIds.

> Your Money Hops, Even When Wifi Wont

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Expo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Expo-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Native](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Native-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem
Digital payments and Web3 have a massive Achilles' heel: they break the moment the internet goes down.

Whether you are at a crowded music festival with congested cellular towers, in a remote rural area with poor infrastructure, or facing a network outage, the inability to transact digitally brings local commerce to a grinding halt.

Furthermore, pushing Web3 adoption to the masses is incredibly difficult due to the friction of gas fees, the necessity of holding native network tokens, and the absolute requirement of an active internet connection just to sign and broadcast a transaction. Finally, existing "offline" payment concepts fail to address the most critical piece of the puzzle: Merchant Trust. A merchant will not hand over goods if they cannot verify they have been paid.

How HopPay (MeshT) Solves This
HopPay is a decentralized, offline-first payment ecosystem that ensures your money hops, even when the WiFi won't. We make digital finance unstoppable.

📡 True Offline Mesh Networking: We engineered a custom Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh protocol. Users securely sign transactions offline, and these encrypted packages "hop" from one nearby smartphone to another until they reach an internet-connected gateway.
⛽ Zero-Friction Web3 Experience: By integrating EIP-3009 (Gasless Meta-Transactions), users don't need to hold gas tokens or understand blockchain mechanics. Our relayer network natively handles the decentralized submission and covers the gas.
🏦 Real-World Merchant Settlement: We bridge the gap between Web3 and everyday commerce by automating INR fiat payouts (via Decentro + UPI). The customer pays in crypto offline, and the merchant settles directly into their bank account.
💬 Closing the Trust Loop: Recognizing that merchants need immediate verification, we integrated serverless SMS confirmations (via Twilio). Even if the merchant's POS device is offline, our relayer triggers a familiar, bank-style SMS to their phone the second the mesh network confirms the transaction, guaranteeing absolute trust.
With HopPay, we are making digital transactions universally accessible, un-censorable, and completely independent of centralized telecom infrastructure.

**FinTech**

Our project directly tackles one of the biggest hurdles in global financial inclusion: the dependence on continuous internet connectivity for digital payments. We fit perfectly into the FinTech track because we have built a resilient, decentralized payment infrastructure that operates seamlessly in internet dead zones.

Here is how we are pushing the boundaries of accessible financial technology:

1. Offline-to-Online Financial Bridging We enable users to locally sign and broadcast transactions entirely offline using a custom Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh protocol. Transactions securely "hop" from device to device until they reach an internet-connected gateway, enabling reliable digital commerce even in remote areas, crowded events, or during network outages.

2. Seamless Blockchain Abstraction By leveraging EIP-3009 for gasless meta-transactions, users can sign transactions offline without needing native gas tokens. Our dedicated relayer network picks up these transactions and handles the submission and gas fees on supported chains (Flow, Hedera, Ethereum), completely abstracting the complexity of Web3 away from the end-user.

3. Real-World Merchant Settlement (Fiat Off-Ramps) Recognizing that scalable FinTech must integrate with local economies, our relayer is designed to handle automated INR fiat payouts (via Decentro + UPI) directly to merchants. A user can pay in crypto offline, and the merchant settles in fiat seamlessly.

4. Bank-Grade Trust & Feedback Trust is critical in finance. To ensure merchants feel secure accepting offline payments, we integrated Twilio to trigger direct, serverless SMS confirmations instantly. This provides a familiar, bank-like notification experience to the merchant's phone the moment a transaction is processed.

By combining offline BLE mesh networks, uncompromising cryptographic security, and seamless fiat off-ramps, we are building the next generation of inclusive, unstoppable financial infrastructure.

**The problem it solves**

## What Cyphron Does

Cyphron catches money mule networks in real time something no existing AML system does reliably.

Traditional fraud tools look at accounts one by one, run overnight batch jobs, and miss coordinated rings entirely. By the time they flag something, the money is gone.

Cyphron instead models the **network**. Every account, device, and IP becomes a node. Every transaction is an edge. A Graph Neural Network scores entire clusters not individuals detecting fan-out, layering, structuring, and U-turn patterns the moment they form, across UPI, ATM, mobile, and web simultaneously.

When a ring is confirmed:
- The cluster is **frozen** in under 500ms
- The analyst gets a **visual graph** showing exactly why it was flagged
- A full **STR report** is auto-drafted by Gemini AI in ~90 seconds

What used to take a compliance team a full day now takes 15 minutes and happens before the money moves, not after.

**Challenges we ran into**

- firestore credits rans out
- merge conflicts
- team members fell sick

> Decentralized P2P Mesh Communication Gateway

![Arduino IDE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino%20IDE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kivy](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kivy-333333?style=flat-square) ![ESP-32 WiFi Module](https://img.shields.io/badge/ESP--32%20WiFi%20Module-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Solution: AKON Disaster Mesh
AKON (Agnostic Communication Node) is a low-power, long-range decentralized network designed to keep people connected when everything else fails [cite: 2026-03-23].

1. Hyper-Local Emergency Messaging
People can use AKON to send "Shouts" (broadcasts) or direct messages to neighbors and rescue teams without needing a SIM card or WiFi.

Use Case: A person trapped in a flooded area can "Shout" their location and medical needs to any node within range.

2. Off-Grid Reliability
Because the system is powered by a rechargeable 18650 battery and an ESP32, it can run for days on a single charge.

How it makes tasks safer: Rescue workers can set up "Gateways" in remote areas to coordinate searches without carrying heavy satellite equipment.

3. Extended Range via LoRa
By using LoRa (Long Range) radio technology instead of standard WiFi, AKON can send text data over kilometers rather than meters [cite: 2026-03-23].

How it makes tasks easier: It allows for a "daisy-chain" (mesh) effect where messages hop from one node to another until they reach a functioning command center

**Challenges we ran into**

4. Hardware Safety (The LoRa Power Trap)The Challenge: The LoRa SX1278 radio is extremely sensitive; it operates at $3.3\text{V}$ and can be destroyed if connected to the booster's $5\text{V}$ output [cite: 2026-03-23].The Solution: I utilized the ESP32’s internal regulator [cite: 2026-03-23]. Instead of powering the radio from the main battery bus, I routed the power through the ESP32’s 3V3 pin [cite: 2026-03-23]. This ensures the radio gets "clean," regulated power, even as the battery voltage fluctuates [cite: 2026-03-23].

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
Some of the common issues faced by citizens, like garbage dumping, potholes, water leaks, and drainage issues, are not reported, or they are reported very late. This is because it is a very time-consuming and inconvenient task. The citizens have to browse government websites, fill out lengthy forms, and search for the department where they can report the problem.

Our solution will make this task easier for citizens by allowing them to report issues instantly by just uploading a photo of the problem.

How People Can Use It
Citizens can easily open the app, click a photo of the problem, and report it instantly. The app will automatically identify the problem and send it to the relevant department of the government.

They can even keep a track of their problem through a dashboard provided by the app.

How It Makes Things Easier and Safer
• Reduces the time required for reporting from minutes to just a few seconds
• Eliminates the need for manual department identification
• Motivates more citizens to report environmental issues
• Enables authorities to address issues more quickly
• Promotes a clean environment and prevents environmental damage
• Prevents minor issues from turning into bigger safety hazards
Overall Impact
By making reporting simple and accessible, the system increases citizen participation and helps cities become cleaner, safer, and more environmentally sustainable.

**Challenges we ran into**

Some of the challenges that we faced during the development of the project are as follows:

1. Accurate Image Detection
The major challenge that we faced during the development of the project was to ensure that the AI system correctly identified the various kinds of issues that are related to the civic and environmental conditions from the images.

How we solved it:
To solve the problem of accurate image detection, we made the input images clearer by providing better images and improving the model prompts. Rather than creating a complex model from scratch, we made the most of the available vision APIs and concentrated more on improving the classification.

2. Issues Mapping to the Correct Department
The second challenge that we faced during the development of the project was related to the mapping of the issues to the correct department.

How we solved it:
To solve the problem of mapping the issues to the correct department, we came up with a simple rule-based system where each issue type is mapped to the correct department.
3. Automating Complaint Generation
The generation of a complaint in a structured form from an image was a tricky issue to solve, particularly in terms of ensuring that it was natural and meaningful.

How we solved it:
The application of AI in text generation using templates was used in this case. This ensured that the complaints were not only structured but also natural and meaningful.

4. Time Constraints
The fact that this was a hackathon meant that there was limited time to complete this project.

How we solved it:
The focus was on developing a working prototype rather than an actual product.

5. Integration of Multiple Components
The integration of multiple aspects in this project was another issue we had to solve.

How we solved it:
The breaking down of this system into smaller units was an effective way to integrate it.

Summary
The problems we faced in this project were instrumental in improving our approach to problem-solving and ensuring that we developed a viable product in this case. The breaking down of complex problems was an effective way to solve this project successfully.

**Environmental Sustainability**

Our project contributes to environmental sustainability by helping identify and resolve environmental issues faster.

It allows users to report problems like garbage dumping, plastic waste, water leaks, and drainage blockages using a simple photo. Faster reporting means quicker action, reducing pollution and environmental damage.

The platform also provides data on waste hotspots and problem areas, helping authorities plan better waste management and resource usage.

By encouraging community participation and enabling smarter city management, the system supports cleaner environments, reduces resource wastage, and promotes sustainable urban development.

**The problem it solves**

India's small business ecosystem is unlike anywhere else in the world. There are 60 million micro, small, and medium businesses operating across the country — home bakers, saree shops, tiffin services, spare parts dealers, boutique tailors, electronics repair shops, wholesale distributors, local grocery stores, and thousands of other categories. Together they contribute nearly 30% of India's GDP and employ over 110 million people.

But here's what makes them unique: they don't run on software. They run on WhatsApp.
A saree shop owner in Coimbatore manages her entire business through a single WhatsApp number. Her customers DM her product photos, place orders in voice notes, negotiate prices in broken Tanglish, and send UPI screenshots as payment proof. A home baker in Chennai takes custom cake orders through WhatsApp at 11pm, manually tracks them in a notebook, and calls customers the next morning to confirm. A spare parts dealer in Surat has 12 different supplier groups and 8 customer broadcast lists — all on WhatsApp — and somehow keeps track of inventory in his head.

This isn't a niche. This is the default operating model for the majority of Indian small businesses. WhatsApp isn't a communication tool for them. It is their ERP, CRM, storefront, order management system, and payment tracker — all in one chat window.

**Challenges we ran into**

WhatsApp's Walled GardenWhatsApp is the most used app in India but the most hostile platform for builders. The official Business API costs money, requires Meta business verification, and takes days to approve. During a hackathon you don't have days. You use the Twilio sandbox — which requires every test user to manually send a join code before they can interact with the bot.That single friction point nearly killed our demo. A judge picking up their phone and typing "join silver-tiger" before experiencing the product destroys the zero-friction narrative we were selling. We built the entire product around the promise of no behavior change, and the platform itself forced behavior change as the first step.


We assumed that if the bot worked well, adoption would follow. That assumption is wrong.The real barrier isn't technical capability — it's trust. A 45-year-old saree shop owner in Coimbatore who has run her business on instinct and relationships for 20 years is not going to hand her customer conversations to a bot she doesn't understand. What if it says something wrong to a loyal customer? What if it misquotes a price? What if it confirms an order she can't fulfill?The fear isn't irrational. It's based on real stakes. Her business is her family's livelihood. A single bad automated response to a long-standing customer could damage a relationship that took years to build. No amount of "AI-powered" messaging overcomes that fear without significant handholding, proof, and time.


Supporting Tamil and Hindi sounds like a feature. The reality is that Indian business communication is a fluid, constantly shifting mix that no model handles cleanly.
Customers don't write in clean Tamil. They write in Tanglish — Tamil words in English script, mixed with numbers, abbreviations, and slang that changes by city and age group. "1 cake venum bro, chocolate wala, tomorrow evening ok ah?" is a completely normal order message. It has Tamil grammar, English words, Hindi influence, and zero punctuation.
Groq's Llama handles this better than most models but still stumbles on hyper-local expressions, specific regional product names, and phonetic spellings of Tamil words in English. "Paal kova" and "pal kova" and "milk sweet" might all mean the same product — the model needs to know that. Training that contextual knowledge at scale, for every Indian language and regional dialect, is a problem that isn't solved yet.
